D013-D008_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for about five months now. Some days, getting out of bed feels impossible, like there’s just this heavy cloud inside me. I used to care about my job—running the branch keeps me busy, or at least it used to—but lately, I’ve stopped caring. I sit at my desk, and even simple decisions take forever. My team has noticed how slow I’ve become, how quiet. I’ll answer questions, but it takes me a while to respond. I’ve started thinking I’m no good to anyone—like I’ve failed my team, my family… my husband doesn’t deserve this.  

There have been times—especially at night—I can’t shut my mind off. Not in a happy way. There was this one weekend where I barely slept, pacing, cleaning, writing lists, feeling restless, like I had to *do* something. It wasn’t enjoyable—more like being wired. It passed in a few days, though. Not sure what caused it.  

The worst part is I’ve thought about how things could end. I’ve imagined driving out to the lake late at night, leaving the car running in the garage. It scares me, but it also feels like the only way out sometimes. I haven’t told anyone, not even my doctor.
D013-D008_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D013-D008_h001.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling completely hollow for about five months now—like there’s just… nothing inside. Some days I don’t even feel sadness, which sounds weird, but it’s like I’m disconnected from everything. I work nights at a data center, so my schedule’s always flipped, but lately I’ve been so restless during downtime, I can’t sit still. I pace the server aisles, fidget with cables, pick at my hands until they’re raw. It’s not like I mean to, I just can’t help it.

I keep replaying little things—like turning off a non-essential server an hour late last week—and I end up thinking I ruined something massive, that I should be fired or punished. It feels way out of proportion, but the guilt sticks. And I catch myself thinking, “Wouldn’t it be easier if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow?” Not that I’d ever act on it—just… a relief from the weight.

There were a couple of weeks a few months back where I felt wired all the time, barely slept, and started drafting this wild idea for a tech startup. But it fizzled fast, and no one said I was manic—just “stressed” or “driven.” I don’t know what I am now. Just… stuck.
D013-D008_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D013-D008_h002.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h003.question:
I’ve been off for about five months now—ever since the last big call, maybe even before that. It’s like I’m moving through fog. Emotions? They’re just… flat. My wife says I don’t react to anything—not the good, not the bad. I love her, I know I do, but I can’t feel it. 

I can’t sit still, either. At home, I pace. In the truck, I fidget, pick at my hands until they’re raw. It’s like my body won’t listen. And the thoughts—man, the thoughts. I keep thinking I caused that collapse last year. I wasn’t the one who missed the signs, but I *should’ve* known. I see the faces of people I’ve never even met and feel responsible. Like the world’s pain is mine to carry.

Sometimes, out of nowhere, I get this sudden pull—like if I stand near a rooftop or on a bridge, this urge hits me hard: *Just jump.* No plan, no real intention, but it’s strong. Scary. 

There were a few weeks where I barely slept but felt wired, talking fast, convinced I could fix everything if I just moved fast enough. But it didn’t last. Just a spark, then back under. I don’t know what’s wrong—just that I can’t function, and I don’t know who I am anymore.
D013-D008_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D013-D008_h003.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h004.question:
I’ve been feeling just… heavy, for about five months now. Some days, getting out of bed feels impossible, like my body doesn’t want to move. When I do, I’m slow—like my thoughts are thick, and it takes forever to answer even simple questions. My husband notices. He’ll ask what I want for dinner and I just stare, trying to form words. 

I feel so guilty—about everything. Last week, I canceled a client’s engagement shoot because I couldn’t face the camera. I kept thinking, “They trusted me, and I ruined everything.” Even though she was kind, I felt like I deserved to be punished. Sometimes I think, “Would anyone even care if I just didn’t wake up?” Not that I’d ever act on it—I’d never hurt my husband like that—but the thought is always there. 

And then, sometimes it flips. A few weeks ago, I stayed up all night editing photos, buzzing with energy, convinced my work was brilliant. But it didn’t last—just crashed back into this fog. It’s happened a couple of times, these bursts. But I don’t know if that means anything. They’re not like full breakdowns or anything—just… spikes. Not enough to call them mania, right? Just me, maybe, trying to keep up.
D013-D008_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D013-D008_h004.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h005.question:
I’ve been feeling... hollow for about five months now, like there’s just nothing inside. Some days, it takes everything just to get out of bed—the shower feels miles away, and even grabbing my keys off the hook feels slow, like my body doesn’t want to listen. At the bank, I make mistakes I never used to: misspelling names, messing up deposits. I used to be good at my job. Now I wonder why they haven’t fired me. I feel useless—like I’m just taking up space. Thoughts cross my mind, like, *I wish I didn’t wake up*, but I wouldn’t actually do anything. It’s just... easier to imagine not being here.

But it hasn’t been all bad, not exactly. There was a stretch last month—maybe two weeks—where I barely slept but didn’t feel tired. I cleaned my apartment at 3 a.m., shopped online, texted old friends out of the blue. Felt sharp, almost high. But it fizzled fast. I don’t know if that counts as anything real. I just know the low feels longer, heavier, and I can’t seem to climb out.
D013-D008_h005.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D013-D008_h006.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about the past two months. Some days, I just can’t get out of bed—there’s no energy, no motivation, and I’ll start crying out of nowhere while I'm just sitting there, staring at the car schematics on my screen. It’s embarrassing. I work in automotive design, so focus is everything, but now I’ll read the same line in an email three times and still not get it. At night, I wake up constantly—usually around 3 or 4 a.m.—and I just lie there, wired but exhausted. 

There are moments, though, especially when I haven’t slept, when everything speeds up. I’ll get these bursts where I feel like I can solve half the project in one night, ideas clicking like gears, hardly needing rest. But it never lasts. And sometimes, when that energy crashes, I get these intense urges—like standing on a footbridge and wondering what it’d feel like to jump. It’s not that I want to, but the thought just *pulls* me. I don’t act on it, but it scares me. I haven’t told anyone. The last thing I need is for them to think I’m unstable at work.
D013-D008_h006.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D013-D008_h006.answer: A & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h007.question:
I’ve been feeling completely hollow inside for about two months now—like there’s no emotion at all, just a flat, empty space. Some days I go through the motions at school, teaching my second graders, but I’m not really *there*. It’s like I’m watching myself from the outside. I can’t focus during lesson planning; my thoughts feel foggy, slow, like I’m wading through mud. Falling asleep takes forever, even when I’m exhausted—my mind races with nothing, just static.  

There are moments—sudden, scary ones—where I get this intense urge, like when I’m standing on the subway platform, a strong impulse to step forward. I don’t have a plan, I don’t want to die, but the thought pops in so sharply it frightens me. I’ve started avoiding the edge without telling anyone.  

My husband says I’ve changed—withdrawn, quiet. I cancel plans, even with close friends. But then, sometimes, for a day or two, I’ll clean the whole house at midnight or start a big project, full of restless energy. It doesn’t feel good, just… *wired*. But it never lasts. I don’t know if it means anything. I just know I’m not myself—and I don’t know how to get back.
D013-D008_h007.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D013-D008_h007.answer: A & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h008.question:

A few weeks ago, I had this burst of energy—started remodeling the garage at 2 a.m., called old clients with grand ideas. But it fizzled fast. My wife said I was “not myself,” but I don’t know what that means anymore. It didn’t last—just left me more drained.
D013-D008_h008.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D013-D008_h009.question:

D013-D008_h010.question:

D013-D008_h011.question:

D013-D008_h012.question:

But… there were a few nights—maybe three or four weeks back—when I didn’t sleep for two, three days straight. I cleaned the whole tower, rewired the old radio for no reason, felt wired, like my thoughts were racing. Felt almost good—until it wasn’t. I don’t know what that was. Maybe just cabin fever. Maybe too much coffee. It passed quick. I just don’t want to lose this job. I need the quiet. But sometimes… the quiet feels too loud.

A. Major Depressive Disorder

D013-D008_h013.question:

D013-D008_h014.question:

D013-D008_h015.question:

D013-D008_h016.question:

D013-D008_h020.question:

I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe a year and a half now. Some weeks, I can’t get out of bed no matter how hard I try. I’ll sleep for 12 hours or more and still feel exhausted, like my brain is wrapped in cotton. I can’t keep track of ideas, and I forget what I just read two sentences ago.

There are days when I cry for no reason—just sitting at my desk, staring at the screen, and suddenly I’m sobbing. I don’t want to burden anyone; I live alone and mostly keep to myself. Now and then, I get these bursts where I stay up late writing, almost frantic, like my mind’s racing ahead of me. I don’t sleep much then, and I feel oddly energized—but it never lasts. It fades fast, and I crash back into this fog. I can’t tell if that’s normal stress or something more. My advisor says I’m overthinking, but it doesn’t feel that simple.
